question: Name the Freedom fighter who formed a clan of non-violent revolutionaries called Khudai Khidmatgars in 1929.
solution:
The correct answer is __Abdul Gaffar Khan.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan organised the “Khudai Khidmatgar” in 1929. 
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan:
 
 
• Abdul Ghaffār Khan, popularly known as Badshah Khan, was a Pashtun independence activist against British colonial rule in India.
 
• He was a political and metaphysical leader known for his nonviolent opposition and lifelong pacifism.
 
• He was a pious Muslim and an advocate for Hindu−Muslim unity in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Due to his identical ideologies and close friendship with Mahatma Gandhi, Khan was nicknamed Sarhadi Gandhi by his close associate Amir Chand Bombwal.
 
• In 1929, Khan established the Khudai Khidmatgar an anti-colonial nonviolent resistance movement.
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgar's prosperity and popularity with the Indian people eventually prompted the British to launch a severe crackdown against him.
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgar undergone some of the most severe repression of the entire Indian independence movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Lal Kurti or Red Shirt Movement was also launched by Abdul Ghaffar Khan in 1930–31.
 
• It is also called the "Khudai Khidmatgar" Movement.
 
• **Khudai Khidmatgar** is a **Persian word** that means in Hindi **'Servant of God'.**
 
• Aim: To support the Civil Disobedience Movement launched by Gandhiji.
 
• The movement opposed the Partition of India.
 
• It was a non-violent movement in which Men wore the Red Shirt and Women wore Black garments.
 
• For this reason, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a Pashtun freedom fighter, in the North-West Frontier Province had conferred the title of Frontier Gandhi.
 
• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, after attending a meeting of the Indian National Congress in 1929, established Khudai Khidmatgar and called for the Red Kurti movement among the Pashtuns.
 
• He was arrested while giving a speech at a gathering in Utmanzai, a town in the N-W Frontier Province.
 
• His first arrest on the charge of rebellion was for 3 years. After that, he got into the habit of facing tortures.
 
• After the arrest of Ghaffar Khan on April 23, 1930, during the Salt Satyagraha, Khidmatgars took out a procession at the Qissa Khwani Bazaar in Peshawar.
 
• The British administration ordered firing and 200 to 250 people died on sight, but there was no reprisal.
